summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout data with good CGM coverage (98.7 percent, 5-minute cadence, largest gap 65 minutes). Overall time in range 86.0 percent, mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL, coefficient of variation 32.6 percent, time above range 8.9 percent, time below range 5.1 percent. Local time is UTC plus 1 hour, verified by comparing hourly_glucose with hourly_glucose_local. The active AAPS profile is confirmed in force: the loop reports carb ratios matching the profile segments in 17 of 18 checkable samples. No carbohydrates were logged in the entire period (0 carb entries, 0 grams, cob equals 0 in all 24 sampled loop statuses), and the user declaration in aaps_profile.analysis_context contains an empty meal_strategies array, so the regimen operates as fully unannounced with UAM coverage only. Two distinct patterns dominate: elevated glucose from 09:00 to 17:00 local (peak hour 16:00, mean 162.8 mg/dL, 32.1 percent above range) and clustered hypoglycemia in two windows, 23:00 to 03:00 local (up to 18.5 percent below range at 01:00) and 18:00 to 19:00 local (7.7 and 15.3 percent below range). Six of 24 therapy response windows fall below 70 mg/dL within 6 hours despite logged boluses of only 0.05 to 0.65 units, indicating the drops originate from loop-driven microboluses and temporary basal rather than from manual dosing.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is 98.7 percent with 3995 valid entries against 4046 expected, 5-minute cadence, no invalid, duplicate or out-of-period entries, 10 gaps and a largest gap of 65 minutes. This supports hourly and daily pattern analysis. The first day (2026-08-07, 33 readings) and last day (2026-08-21, 269 readings) are partial and are excluded from daily comparisons. Local time equals UTC plus 1 hour, independently verified because hourly_glucose_local at hour h equals hourly_glucose at hour h minus 1 for all hours. Profile applicability is confirmed: loop-reported carb ratio matches the profile segment for the corresponding local hour in 17 of 18 checkable samples, with the single exception of the overnight window reporting 13.3 g/U against a profile value of 13.0 g/U, a difference of about 2 percent across 3 samples. Profile completeness is full: 7 basal segments, 5 carb ratio segments, 1 ISF segment, 3 target segments and DIA are all present. The single flat ISF segment is consistent by design with dynamic_sensitivity_enabled set to true and autosens_enabled set to false. Telemetry counts are large (2315 treatments, 6214 device statuses) but only 40 representative treatments and 24 representative loop statuses are included, so the microbolus and temporary basal stream is sampled rather than complete. Insulin totals are 655 entries and 275.95 units over 14 days, an average of 0.42 units per entry, consistent with heavy microbolus use.
analysis_steps.evidence: telemetry.data_quality; telemetry.daily_glucose rows for 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-21; comparison of telemetry.hourly_glucose and telemetry.hourly_glucose_local; carb ratio values inside representative_loop_statuses reason strings compared with aaps_profile.carb_ratio_segments; telemetry.treatment_summary; telemetry.included_counts; aaps_profile.
analysis_steps.dependencies: None. All later stages inherit the timezone mapping, the confirmed profile applicability, and the identified data gaps.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate entries anywhere in the package. No complete microbolus and temporary basal timeline, only a 40-item representative sample. It is unclear whether total_insulin_u of 275.95 includes basal delivery, so daily total insulin cannot be stated precisely. Insulin peak time is not supplied, only insulin_type equal to free_peak_oref. No activity or exercise log beyond temporary targets.

analysis_steps.findings: Time below range is 5.1 percent for the period, above the commonly cited 4 percent ceiling, while time in range is 86.0 percent and coefficient of variation is 32.6 percent, which is below the 36 percent variability threshold. Two sustained level-2 hypoglycemia clusters are present and appear genuine because each spans several consecutive readings: 2026-08-13 from 17:59 to 18:14 local with values 51, 47, 42 and 45 mg/dL, and 2026-08-14 from 19:04 to 19:14 local with values 48, 41 and 41 mg/dL. A third low of 42 mg/dL on 2026-08-21 at 07:19 local is isolated, occurs on a day with only 0.7 percent below range, and precedes a sensor change at 10:08 local, so a sensor artifact is at least as plausible as a therapy event. Hypoglycemia is strongly time-clustered in local hours 23:00 to 03:00 (10.1, 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent below range) and in local hours 18:00 and 19:00 (7.7 and 15.3 percent). Hyperglycemia is clustered from 10:00 to 17:00 local, peaking at 16:00 with 32.1 percent above range and a mean of 162.8 mg/dL. A recurring overcorrection signature is visible in therapy_response_windows: 172 to 47 mg/dL at 240 minutes, 234 to 56 mg/dL at 120 minutes, 264 to 96 mg/dL at 120 minutes, 206 to 53 mg/dL at 180 minutes, and 125 to 57 mg/dL at 240 minutes, in each case from a logged bolus of only 0.05 to 0.65 units. Six of 24 windows fall below 70 mg/dL within 6 hours. Observed insulin on board reaches 5.935 units against a max_iob limit of 25 units, and negative insulin on board of minus 0.481, minus 0.197 and minus 0.159 units appears after prolonged zero temporary basal. Confounders within the period include occlusion and pump error announcements on 2026-08-19 at 14:40 local, site changes on 08-10, 08-13 and 08-17, sensor changes on 08-11 and 08-21, a profile switch on 08-13, and GLP-1 1.25 mg on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20, that is every three days.
analysis_steps.evidence: telemetry.glucose_summary; telemetry.daily_glucose; telemetry.hourly_glucose_local; telemetry.glucose_extremes; telemetry.therapy_response_windows; telemetry.representative_events; telemetry.representative_loop_statuses.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on the timezone mapping and the sampling limitation established in data_quality. Constrains every later stage: no proposal may increase insulin delivery in the 22:00 to 03:00 or 18:00 to 20:00 local windows, and any fix for afternoon highs must be judged by its evening hypoglycemia consequence.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The proportion of pre-hypoglycemia insulin delivered as microbolus versus temporary basal cannot be determined from the representative sample. No hypoglycemia treatment or rescue carbohydrate records exist, so the true depth and duration of lows may be masked by unlogged carbohydrates, for example the rebound from 47 to 204 mg/dL between 240 and 360 minutes on 2026-08-13.

analysis_steps.findings: The overnight window from 23:00 to 07:00 local is flat in mean terms (105.7, 93.3, 90.6, 101.9, 104.7, 106.0, 104.2, 99.5, 99.5 mg/dL) with no sustained rise or fall, but the hypoglycemia burden is concentrated in its first hours and then disappears: 10.1, 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent below range from 23:00 to 03:00, against 3.0, 4.8, 2.5 and 1.3 percent from 04:00 to 07:00, with 95 to 99 percent in range from 04:00 to 08:00. A uniformly excessive 00:00 basal of 0.6 U/h covering 00:00 to 05:00 would be expected to produce lows across the whole segment rather than only its first three hours, so a decaying evening insulin tail under a 10-hour DIA is a better fit than a basal defect. This is supported by the 2026-08-17 21:15 UTC window (125 to 57 mg/dL at 240 minutes from 0.05 units), the 2026-08-12 21:30 UTC window (138 to 82 mg/dL at 240 minutes) and the 2026-08-20 21:04 UTC status showing insulin on board of 2.802 units, minGuardBG of 28 mg/dL and a zero temporary basal already running for 120 minutes. The morning rise from 07:00 to 10:00 local (99.5, 110.5, 132.9, 148.0 mg/dL) is too steep and too meal-shaped to attribute to dawn basal and, with zero carbohydrate entries, is most plausibly unannounced breakfast handled by UAM. In the afternoon the profile places its lowest basal, 0.5 U/h from 16:00 to 18:00, in the hour with the highest mean glucose and the highest time above range. This is a genuine face-value mismatch, but the same window is immediately followed by the highest evening hypoglycemia burden, so total insulin arriving in the late afternoon is already sufficient or excessive and mainly mistimed; raising basal there would most plausibly deepen the 18:00 and 19:00 lows. On targets, the profile declares only 90, 100 and 90 mg/dL, yet loop target_bg values across the 24 samples are 80, 84, 86, 87, 90, 97, 99, 101, 104, 105, 106, 108 and 116 mg/dL. This modulation is examined further in the sensitivity stage.
analysis_steps.evidence: telemetry.hourly_glucose_local hours 18 through 07; telemetry.therapy_response_windows entries dated 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-17; representative_loop_statuses dated 2026-08-20T21:04:53Z; aaps_profile.basal_segments and aaps_profile.target_segments; decision_inventory profile rows.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on data_quality for the timezone mapping and profile applicability, and on safety_overview for the two hypoglycemia windows. The overnight hypothesis depends on the DIA and insulin-on-board assessment in profile_cr_isf_dia. The afternoon hypothesis cannot be separated from meal effects until the meal stages.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate entries, so meal effects cannot be subtracted from any hourly window. No complete microbolus and temporary basal record, so delivered basal cannot be compared with profile basal hour by hour. No fasting or basal-test day is identifiable in the data. The mechanism producing effective targets between 80 and 116 mg/dL is not documented in the supplied settings.

analysis_steps.findings: The five carb ratio segments are not verifiable in this period. With zero carbohydrate entries there is no announced-meal outcome anywhere in the package, so none of the values 13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5 and 12.6 g/U has ever influenced a meal bolus. The only carb ratio evidence is that the loop reads the profile correctly, with one 2 percent overnight discrepancy noted in data_quality. ISF is a single flat 56 mg/dL/U segment used as the base for dynamic sensitivity at 70 percent. Effective variable_sens across the 24 sampled statuses spans 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U and is strongly glucose dependent: around 108 to 124 mg/dL/U at glucose near 84 to 98 mg/dL, around 53 to 95 mg/dL/U at glucose near 120 to 150 mg/dL, and 27.8 to 43.2 mg/dL/U at glucose above roughly 170 mg/dL. The most aggressive samples coincide with the crash precursors: 2026-08-19 at 15:54 UTC with glucose 262 mg/dL, insulin on board 4.73 units, sensitivity 37.9 mg/dL/U, insulinReq 1.98 units and a reason string stating UAM High Boost enacted with a microbolus of 1.6 units, followed by a fall from 264 to 96 mg/dL in 120 minutes; and 2026-08-21 at 21:09 UTC with glucose 245.7 mg/dL, insulin on board 5.935 units, sensitivity 27.8 mg/dL/U and insulinReq 2.12 units. Because profile ISF and the dynamic factor multiply into the same effective number, they cannot be separated on the present evidence. DIA is 10 hours with insulin_type free_peak_oref. A long DIA extends the insulin tail and is mechanistically consistent with the late evening and overnight lows and with the repeated declines at 240 and 360 minutes after very small logged boluses, for example minus 68 mg/dL at 240 minutes from 0.05 units and minus 67 and minus 66 mg/dL at 240 and 360 minutes from 0.2 units. It also explains the recurrent negative insulin on board after long zero temporary basals. However DIA is confounded with dynamic sensitivity aggressiveness, with the unsupplied insulin peak time, and with microbolus stacking at a 3-minute interval, and no isolated DIA test exists in the data.
analysis_steps.evidence: variable_sens, sensitivity_ratio, insulin_req, iob and reason strings across all 24 representative_loop_statuses; telemetry.therapy_response_windows entries dated 2026-08-11, 2026-08-14, 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-19; aaps_profile.isf_segments, aaps_profile.dia_hours and aaps_profile.carb_ratio_segments; aaps_profile.smb_settings.raw_settings.dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on basal_targets, because both hypoglycemia clusters route through the insulin-on-board tail. Depends on safety_overview for the overcorrection signature. The competing explanations of effective sensitivity, DIA and microbolus sizing must be separated in the automation stages before any change is proposed.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No announced carbohydrate outcomes, so carb ratio remains untestable. Insulin peak time is not supplied. No microbolus-resolution insulin timeline, so the 2 to 4 hour declines cannot be attributed between microbolus and high temporary basal. GLP-1 dosed every three days may shift both absorption and sensitivity within the window and cannot be quantified here.

analysis_steps.findings: Microbolus and UAM are both enabled and are the only mechanism covering meals, because carbohydrates are never announced and cob equals 0 in all sampled statuses. UAM is not duplicating carbohydrate-on-board counting here, since carbohydrate-on-board is genuinely zero throughout. Disabling either would remove all meal coverage and is unsupported. The activation conditions are internally coherent: smb_always_enabled set to true makes smb_with_cob_enabled and smb_after_carbs_enabled inert in the current data, and smb_with_temp_target_enabled true combined with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false means microboluses are suppressed while a high temporary target runs. The user ran 135 mg/dL temporary targets for 180 minutes on 2026-08-17 at 12:30 UTC and 2026-08-18 at 14:24 UTC, and 2026-08-18 is simultaneously the day with the highest time below range at 12.8 percent and one of the highest above range at 15.3 percent. This is deliberate-looking behavior rather than a defect, but it means microbolus delivery is intermittently off and must be accounted for before concluding that microbolus dosing is uniformly too aggressive. On strength and frequency, the configured 3-minute interval is a standard value taken from the setting itself and not from any waiting message. The configured caps compute as 15 minutes times basal 0.7 to 0.8 U/h, equal to 0.18 to 0.20 units, and 20 minutes times 0.7 to 0.8 U/h, equal to 0.23 to 0.27 units, and the loop reports exactly these as standardMaxBolus, 0.2 units on 2026-08-07 and 0.3 units on 2026-08-10. Delivery nevertheless exceeds them: on 2026-08-07 the reason string reads insulinReq 0.47, standardMaxBolus 0.2, Microbolusing 0.4U, which is twice the configured cap; on 2026-08-18 the string reads Increased SMB as percentage with insulinReq 1.45; and on 2026-08-19 the string reads UAM High Boost enacted, SMB equals 1.6. A material completeness concern follows: the running build reports Enhanced oref1, UAM Boost 1 and UAM Boost 2 values up to 35.93, UAM High Boost, prTrial, twin, antBackout, accelMeal and a G3 pre-UAM uncertainty hold, and none of these boost parameters appear in the supplied smb_settings. The six supplied AAPS groups therefore do not fully describe the delivery logic, so the predicted effect of reducing the basal-minute caps is uncertain. Remaining raw settings, including insulin_type, bolus_wizard_percentage, max_allowed_bolus_units, max_allowed_carbs_grams, min_carbs_required_grams, sensitivity_algorithm and short_average_delta_enabled, were audited and are unremarkable.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.smb_settings and raw_settings; standardMaxBolus and Microbolusing values in representative_loop_statuses dated 2026-08-07, 2026-08-10, 2026-08-18 and 2026-08-19; representative_events temporary target entries dated 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18; daily_glucose row for 2026-08-18; telemetry.treatment_summary.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on safety_overview for the overcorrection signature, on basal_targets for the timing of the two hypoglycemia clusters, and on profile_cr_isf_dia because microbolus size, effective sensitivity and DIA are three routes to the same outcome and must not be changed together.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The boost multipliers that override standardMaxBolus are not present in the supplied settings, so the magnitude of any cap reduction cannot be predicted. The representative treatment sample does not allow reconstruction of microbolus frequency or cumulative microbolus dose per window.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is disabled, dynamic sensitivity is enabled at 70 percent, and both autosens target adjustments are false. Observed sensitivity_ratio values are 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94, 0.98 and 1.0; a ratio of 1 is read as a neutral current adjustment and not as a disabled function. Effective sensitivity spans 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U around a flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, so the running sensitivity is roughly twice as strong as the profile above 200 mg/dL and roughly half as strong below 100 mg/dL. Effective targets also move: whenever sensitivity_ratio is below 1 the target rises above profile (0.79 with target 116, 0.88 with 108, 0.91 with 106, 0.92 with 105, 0.94 with 104, 0.98 with 101 mg/dL), and whenever the ratio is 1 with high or rising glucose the target falls to 80 to 90 mg/dL against a profile target of 100 mg/dL in those local hours, seen at 138.8, 169, 245.7 and 262 mg/dL. The declared components state that autosens does not raise or lower the target, so the declared settings and the observed behavior do not agree, and the most likely explanation is target modulation inside the custom boost branch rather than a settings error. The practical consequence is multiplicative: a working target of 80 mg/dL with an effective sensitivity of 27.8 mg/dL/U produced insulinReq of 2.12 units on top of 5.935 units already on board. On the safety limits, max_iob of 25 units stands against 275.95 units of bolus and microbolus insulin over 14 days, about 19.7 units per day, and a peak observed insulin on board of 5.935 units. The ceiling is roughly one to two days of insulin and is never approached, so lowering it would not alter routine dosing but would restore a meaningful backstop against a runaway boost sequence. Importantly, max_basal of 12 U/h is not the binding constraint: the logs show adj. req. rate 5.9 to maxSafeBasal 4 on 2026-08-14 and enacted rates of 3.2, 3.6 and 4.0 U/h, so the real ceiling comes from max_daily_safety_multiplier of 5 times the maximum profile basal of 0.8 U/h, equal to 4.0 U/h, with current_basal_safety_multiplier of 6 times 0.7 U/h giving 4.2 U/h. Both multipliers sit above common defaults and permit temporary basal at five to six times profile basal, which occurred immediately before the 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-19 events. This is recorded as a safety observation rather than a routine optimization. The carbohydrate absorption group, min_5m_carbimpact of 8 mg/dL per 5 minutes and meal_max_absorption_hours of 7 hours, was never exercised because carbohydrate-on-board was zero in every sampled status, so the package contains no evidence on either value.
analysis_steps.evidence: variable_sens, sensitivity_ratio and target_bg pairs across all 24 representative_loop_statuses; reason strings dated 2026-08-14T18:40Z and 2026-08-19T15:54Z; aaps_profile.smb_settings.raw_settings max_iob_units, max_basal_u_per_hour, max_daily_safety_multiplier, current_basal_safety_multiplier, autosens_enabled, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent, min_5m_carbimpact and meal_max_absorption_hours; telemetry.treatment_summary; aaps_profile.basal_segments.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on all earlier stages. Profile ISF, the dynamic sensitivity factor and the UAM microbolus cap are three levers acting on the same effective dose, so at most one may move at a time. The max_iob limit is the only lever independent of every other setting and therefore can be sequenced first without confounding any later test.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The mechanism and configuration of the observed target modulation between 80 and 116 mg/dL are not present in the supplied settings, so its magnitude cannot be predicted or directly adjusted. Insulin peak time is unsupplied. No carbohydrate-on-board was ever created, so both absorption settings remain untested.

analysis_steps.findings: The user declaration in aaps_profile.analysis_context is present and user-sourced, declared at 2026-08-21T21:08:10Z, but meal_strategies is an empty array, period_exceptions is null and strategy_stable_for_period is null. Because strategy_stable_for_period is not true, no representative declaration can be assigned to the period, and every statement below is inference from glucose and insulin telemetry at correspondingly reduced confidence. Telemetry agrees with the declaration: zero carbohydrate entries, zero grams, all 24 therapy response windows are correction boluses with is_extended_carbs false, and cob equals 0 in every sampled status. Three recurring unannounced intake windows are visible in local time. Morning from 08:00 to 10:00 rises 110.5 to 132.9 to 148.0 mg/dL with time above range moving 1.8 to 8.9 to 20.2 percent and time below range of 0.0, 0.0 and 1.2 percent. Afternoon from 12:00 to 17:00 forms a broad plateau of 141.3, 135.0, 148.1, 153.0, 162.8 and 148.9 mg/dL with time above range from 14.0 to 32.1 percent and no single sharp peak. Evening from 20:00 to 22:00 rises modestly to 117.0, 120.0 and 127.6 mg/dL. Individual windows corroborate: 100 to 188 mg/dL in 60 minutes on 2026-08-14, 126 to 190 mg/dL by 180 minutes on 2026-08-17, 164 to 205 mg/dL in 60 minutes on 2026-08-19 and 142 to 187 mg/dL in 60 minutes on 2026-08-20. The operating strategy is therefore fully reactive: no prebolus, no immediate bolus fraction, and UAM must detect a rise before dosing, which explains the daytime highs as a strategy consequence rather than a basal or carb ratio defect. Because carbohydrate-on-board never exists, every meal is handled as a correction against unattributed rising glucose, so effective sensitivity and the modulated target carry the entire meal load, which is why the catch-up requests reach 1.98 and 2.12 units. Hypoglycemia risk is asymmetric by window: the morning carries essentially none (0.0, 0.0 and 1.2 percent below range) while the afternoon precedes the highest evening lows.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.analysis_context with meal_strategies as an empty array; telemetry.carb_treatment_entries as an empty array; telemetry.treatment_summary carb_entries 0 and total_carbs_g 0.0; cob values across representative_loop_statuses; telemetry.hourly_glucose_local hours 08 through 22; therapy_response_windows dated 2026-08-14, 2026-08-17, 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-20.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate amounts or entry timestamps exist, so prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage and carb ratio accuracy cannot be measured. Meal composition is unknown and is not inferred. GLP-1 every three days is an unquantifiable confounder on absorption speed.

analysis_steps.findings: No extended carbohydrate evidence exists in the package. extended_carb_entries is 0, average_extended_carb_duration_min is null, carb_treatment_entries is an empty array and is_extended_carbs is false in all 24 therapy response windows. No extended carbohydrate amount, start offset, duration or absorption outcome can be assessed, and none is invented. Two structural observations are recorded without becoming recommendations. First, the afternoon plateau from 12:00 to 17:00 local has the extended shape for which extended carbohydrate entries are conceptually intended, but that shape is equally explainable by repeated small unlogged intake or by delayed gastric emptying under GLP-1 dosed every three days on 2026-08-14, 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-20, and the meal, insulin-on-board, microbolus, temporary-target and correction effects cannot be separated with the data present. No duration is inferred from any aggregate average. Second, extended carbohydrate entries are not a pump extended bolus: they create carbohydrate-on-board over a declared duration so the absorption model can act, and they do not schedule insulin delivery directly. That distinction matters here because the two absorption settings that would govern them, min_5m_carbimpact of 8 and meal_max_absorption_hours of 7, have never had any carbohydrate-on-board to act upon, so using extended carbohydrates now would activate two never-validated parameters simultaneously and would conflict with sequential single-change validation.

analysis_steps.findings: A contradiction audit against aaps_profile, profile_context and decision_inventory produced three corrections to earlier reasoning. First, the earlier suggestion that the maximum basal limit be treated as part of the same finding as max_iob is not supportable: max_basal of 12 U/h is demonstrably not binding, because the loop caps itself at 4.0 U/h through the safety multipliers, so only max_iob within that group has a supported change. Second, the earlier framing that microbolus caps are a clean lever is downgraded, because the reason strings prove delivery exceeds standardMaxBolus through boost logic that is absent from the supplied settings, so the effect of reducing max_uam_smb_basal_minutes is not predictable and it must not be the first change. Third, the observed target modulation contradicts the declared autosens target settings; this conflict is reported rather than resolved in favor of either source, and confidence is lowered accordingly. Competing explanations were then ranked. The daytime highs from 09:00 to 17:00 local are best explained by fully reactive UAM coverage of unannounced meals, not by the 0.5 U/h basal at 16:00; raising that basal is rejected because the same insulin would land in the 18:00 and 19:00 window that already carries 7.7 and 15.3 percent time below range. The evening lows are best explained by afternoon overcorrection, because the logged boluses of 0.05 to 0.65 units cannot produce falls of 168 to 178 mg/dL, so the insulin came from boosted microboluses and temporary basal up to 4 U/h. The overnight lows from 23:00 to 03:00 are best explained by the decaying insulin tail under a 10-hour DIA rather than by excess 00:00 basal, because time below range collapses to 1.3 to 4.8 percent from 04:00 to 07:00 while basal is unchanged, but this remains partially unresolved and no basal change is therefore proposed. The single mechanism common to every documented crash is the multiplication of a lowered effective target, an effective sensitivity steepened to 27.8 to 43.2 mg/dL/U at high glucose, and boosted microbolus delivery. Ranking the available levers by independence gives a clear safe order: max_iob is the only lever that confounds nothing and is never reached in normal operation, so it is first; the dynamic sensitivity factor is the single most direct influence on high-glucose aggressiveness and is second, alone; profile ISF and the UAM microbolus cap are held in reserve because each would confound the sensitivity test; carbohydrate logging is a data-collection action rather than a dose change and can run in parallel with observation but not with a dose change; and no basal, carb ratio, target, DIA or absorption change is supported by this package.
analysis_steps.evidence: Synthesis of all preceding stages against aaps_profile, profile_context, decision_inventory and telemetry; specifically hourly_glucose_local, therapy_response_windows, representative_loop_statuses variable_sens, target_bg, insulin_req and iob values, treatment_summary, and raw_settings max_iob_units, max_basal_u_per_hour, max_daily_safety_multiplier and current_basal_safety_multiplier.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on all eight preceding stages. The sequencing rule that follows is that only one insulin-delivery setting changes at a time, with a full observation period between changes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Boost and target-modulation parameters absent from the supplied settings; no carbohydrate data; insulin peak time unsupplied; microbolus and temporary basal stream only sampled. These gaps cap overall confidence at medium and are the reason no profile change is proposed.

strengths: Data quality: CGM coverage of 98.7 percent with a consistent 5-minute cadence, zero invalid entries, zero duplicates and a largest gap of only 65 minutes. This is high-quality data that supports hourly pattern analysis without qualification.

Overall control: time in range of 86.0 percent with a mean glucose of 121.6 mg/dL is achieved while never announcing a single carbohydrate, which reflects a well-functioning automated system and consistent engagement.

Variability: coefficient of variation of 32.6 percent sits below the commonly used 36 percent stability threshold, indicating that glucose swings are contained despite the fully unannounced meal approach.

Overnight and dawn: the window from 04:00 to 08:00 local is excellent, with 95.2 to 98.7 percent in range, 1.3 to 4.8 percent below range and zero time above range, indicating the late-night and dawn basal shape is well matched in that segment.

Profile consistency: the active profile is demonstrably in force, with loop-reported carb ratios matching the profile segments in 17 of 18 checkable samples, so profile-based reasoning rests on a verified foundation.

Engagement: site changes, sensor changes, profile switches, GLP-1 doses and temporary targets are consistently recorded, which allowed several glucose excursions to be attributed to context rather than misread as therapy defects.
issues: Safety: time below range is 5.1 percent for the period, above the commonly cited 4 percent ceiling, and includes two sustained level-2 clusters: 51, 47, 42 and 45 mg/dL on 2026-08-13 from 17:59 to 18:14 local, and 48, 41 and 41 mg/dL on 2026-08-14 from 19:04 to 19:14 local.

Safety: a recurring overcorrection pattern is present, with six of 24 therapy response windows falling below 70 mg/dL within 6 hours and falls of 168 to 178 mg/dL following logged boluses of only 0.2 to 0.65 units, so the delivered insulin came predominantly from loop-driven microboluses and temporary basal.

Sensitivity: effective sensitivity ranges from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U around a flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, becoming roughly twice as strong as profile above 200 mg/dL, and the strongest values coincide exactly with the crash on 2026-08-19 and the unresolved high-insulin state on 2026-08-21.

Target: loop target values span 80 to 116 mg/dL while the profile declares only 90, 100 and 90 mg/dL, and targets fall to 80 mg/dL during high and rising glucose although autosens_lowers_target is declared false. Declared settings and observed behavior conflict, most plausibly through target modulation in the custom boost branch.

Safety limits: max_iob of 25 units stands against roughly 19.7 units of bolus and microbolus insulin per day and a peak observed insulin on board of 5.935 units, so the limit is never approached and currently provides no practical backstop against a runaway boost sequence.

Safety limits: the effective temporary basal ceiling is set by max_daily_safety_multiplier of 5 and current_basal_safety_multiplier of 6 rather than by max_basal of 12 U/h, permitting 4.0 to 4.2 U/h, which is five to six times profile basal and was reached immediately before the 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-19 events.

Microbolus delivery: delivery exceeds the configured caps, with standardMaxBolus 0.2 units followed by a 0.4-unit microbolus on 2026-08-07 and a 1.6-unit microbolus on 2026-08-19. The boost parameters responsible are not present in the supplied settings, so the effect of adjusting the basal-minute caps cannot be predicted.

Pattern: daytime hyperglycemia is concentrated from 09:00 to 17:00 local, peaking at 16:00 with a mean of 162.8 mg/dL and 32.1 percent above range, and is best explained by fully reactive UAM coverage of unannounced meals rather than by a basal defect.

Data: no carbohydrates were logged in 14 days and the user declaration contains an empty meal_strategies array, so carb ratio accuracy, prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage and both carbohydrate absorption settings are untestable in this period.

Context: several excursions coincide with device and treatment context rather than settings, including occlusion and pump error on 2026-08-19 at 14:40 local before the 264 mg/dL peak, a sensor change on 2026-08-21 shortly after the isolated 42 mg/dL reading, and GLP-1 1.25 mg every three days, which may shift absorption and sensitivity within the period.

recommendations.title: Discuss reducing max IOB as the first, independent step
recommendations.description: max_iob is currently 25 units while bolus and microbolus insulin averages roughly 19.7 units per day and the highest insulin on board observed in the sampled loop statuses is 5.935 units. The limit is never approached in normal operation, so reducing it would not alter routine dosing, yet it is the only supplied parameter that provides a hard ceiling if the boost logic requests large doses at high glucose, as it did with insulinReq of 1.98 units on 2026-08-19 and 2.12 units on 2026-08-21. This is also the only lever in the whole package that does not confound any later test of basal, sensitivity, DIA, microbolus sizing or meal handling, which is why it belongs first in the sequence. A value in the region of 8 to 10 units would still sit above every observed insulin-on-board value with substantial headroom while restoring a meaningful backstop.

suggested_change.what_to_watch: Whether any loop status is ever constrained by the new limit, and whether time below range in the 18:00 to 19:00 and 23:00 to 03:00 local windows changes.

recommendations.title: Consider the dynamic sensitivity factor as the second, isolated step
recommendations.description: Effective sensitivity steepens to 27.8 to 43.2 mg/dL/U at high glucose against a flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, and every documented crash follows a high-glucose state in which this steepened sensitivity, a lowered effective target and boosted microbolus delivery multiply together. The dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent of 70 is the most direct single influence on that aggressiveness and can be reduced without touching profile ISF, which keeps the low-glucose behavior anchored. This must not be combined with any change to profile ISF or to the microbolus caps, because all three act on the same effective dose and a combined change would make the result uninterpretable. It should only follow a completed max IOB observation period.

suggested_change.what_to_watch: Effective variable_sens values at glucose above 200 mg/dL, the size of insulinReq at high glucose, and time below range at 18:00 and 19:00 local, currently 7.7 and 15.3 percent.

recommendations.title: Raise the safety multipliers with the care team before any other automation change
recommendations.description: The binding temporary basal ceiling is not max_basal of 12 U/h but max_daily_safety_multiplier of 5 and current_basal_safety_multiplier of 6, which together permit 4.0 to 4.2 U/h, five to six times the maximum profile basal of 0.8 U/h. Rates of 3.2, 3.6 and 4.0 U/h were enacted immediately before the events of 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-19. These parameters are outside the six review groups and are raised here only because they change the safe action order: they explain why the max_basal value itself is not worth adjusting, and they are worth reviewing with the care team before concluding that any remaining aggressiveness is caused by sensitivity settings.

suggested_change.reason: These are outside the six reviewable groups and determine the real 4.0 to 4.2 U/h temporary basal ceiling; no value is proposed here.

recommendations.title: Log morning carbohydrates to unblock the meal and carb ratio analysis
recommendations.description: Zero carbohydrates were logged in 14 days, which blocks assessment of all five carb ratio segments, prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage and both carbohydrate absorption settings. Logging the carbohydrate amount and entry time for the morning meal only, between 08:00 and 10:00 local, would produce the first announced-meal outcomes in this dataset. The morning window is the safest place to start because it currently carries 0.0 percent time below range at 08:00 and 09:00 and 1.2 percent at 10:00, so a logging or dosing error there has almost no historical hypoglycemia consequence. This is a data-collection action and not a dose change, so it can run alongside an observation period, but it should not begin in the same week as a settings change if the intent is to attribute the result cleanly.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all seventeen profile rows unchanged for now, including ISF at 56 mg/dL/U, and address high-glucose aggressiveness through the dynamic sensitivity factor in the automation layer instead. The one profile row most likely to matter later is ISF, and it should be held in reserve as the fallback lever if reducing the dynamic factor does not sufficiently reduce the post-high hypoglycemia pattern.
profile_recommendation.rationale: No profile row has evidence that separates it from a more plausible alternative explanation. Basal cannot be changed because the overnight lows are concentrated in 23:00 to 03:00 local while the same basal segment produces 95 to 99 percent time in range from 04:00 to 08:00, which fits a decaying insulin tail rather than a basal excess, and because the afternoon 0.5 U/h segment coincides with the highest glucose but sits directly upstream of the highest evening time below range, so raising it would most plausibly deepen those lows. All five carb ratio segments are untestable, since zero carbohydrates were logged and carbohydrate-on-board was zero in every sampled loop status. Targets should not be changed while the loop is already applying its own modulation between 80 and 116 mg/dL through a mechanism not present in the supplied settings, since a profile target change would interact unpredictably with it. DIA at 10 hours is mechanistically consistent with the late declines at 240 and 360 minutes, but it is confounded with dynamic sensitivity, microbolus stacking at a 3-minute interval and an unsupplied insulin peak time, and no isolated test exists. ISF itself is a flat base value that is deliberately paired with dynamic sensitivity, so the effective sensitivity of 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U is produced by the multiplication of ISF and the 70 percent factor; changing the factor is the cleaner first test because it preserves the low-glucose anchor.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After the max IOB step and then a single reduction of the dynamic sensitivity factor, collect at least 10 days and compare the effective variable_sens values recorded at glucose above 200 mg/dL together with time below range at 18:00 and 19:00 local, currently 7.7 and 15.3 percent. If the high-glucose sensitivity values remain below roughly 40 mg/dL/U and the evening lows persist, revisit profile ISF at 56 mg/dL/U as the next single change.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: this segment covers 00:00 to 05:00 local, where time below range is 11.4, 18.5, 10.1, 10.2 and 3.0 percent for hours 00 through 04, and hourly means are flat at 90.6 to 106.0 mg/dL with no downward drift. Uncertainty: a uniformly excessive basal would depress the whole segment rather than concentrate lows in its first three hours, and the clean 04:00 to 07:00 window under the same and higher basal rates argues against a basal excess. The 2026-08-20 21:04 UTC status showing insulin on board of 2.802 units with a zero temporary basal already running supports a decaying insulin tail instead. Dependencies: this cannot be separated from DIA of 10 hours, from evening correction dosing and from the boost logic until the sensitivity change is tested, so no change is supported now.

Evidence: local hours 05 and 06 show 95.2 and 97.5 percent time in range, 4.8 and 2.5 percent below range and zero percent above range, with stable means of 104.2 and 99.5 mg/dL. Uncertainty: none material; this is one of the best-controlled windows in the dataset. Dependencies: none that would justify change, and altering a well-performing segment would add noise to the planned sequential tests. No change is supported.

Evidence: local hours 06 through 09 show 98.7, 98.2, 91.1 and 78.6 percent time in range with 1.3, 0.0, 0.0 and 1.2 percent below range. The rise begins at 08:00 to 09:00 and reaches a mean of 148.0 by 10:00. Uncertainty: that rise is too steep and too meal-shaped to be attributed to dawn basal, and with zero carbohydrate entries an unannounced breakfast covered reactively by UAM is the more plausible explanation. Dependencies: separating dawn phenomenon from meal effect requires the morning carbohydrate logging recommended separately, so no change is supported until then.

Evidence: local hours 10 through 15 show elevated means of 148.0, 132.3, 141.3, 135.0, 148.1 and 153.0 mg/dL with time above range from 7.5 to 26.3 percent. Uncertainty: this window is dominated by unannounced intake handled reactively by UAM, and the same window is upstream of the evening lows, so a basal increase would risk adding insulin that lands during the 18:00 and 19:00 hypoglycemia window. Dependencies: meal effect, microbolus sizing and target modulation are all unresolved contributors here, so the pattern must not be attributed to basal. No change is supported.

Evidence: this is the profile's lowest basal and it coincides with the day's worst hour, local 16:00 with a mean of 162.8 mg/dL and 32.1 percent above range, which is a genuine face-value mismatch. Uncertainty: the same window is immediately followed by the highest evening time below range, 7.7 percent at 18:00 and 15.3 percent at 19:00, and every documented crash originates here, with falls of 168 to 178 mg/dL from logged boluses of only 0.2 to 0.65 units. That indicates the total insulin arriving in this window is already sufficient or excessive and is mistimed rather than insufficient. Dependencies: raising this segment would conflict with the safety constraint against adding insulin upstream of the 18:00 to 20:00 window and would confound the planned sensitivity test. Reconsider only after the sensitivity change has been observed and if afternoon highs persist without evening lows.

Evidence: local hour 18 shows 7.7 percent below range and 11.9 percent above range with a mean of 124.2 mg/dL, a mixed picture rather than a consistent direction. Uncertainty: the lows in this hour are attributable to the afternoon overcorrection cascade rather than to basal, because the falls of 168 and 178 mg/dL cannot be produced by the logged boluses of 0.2 and 0.65 units. Dependencies: a basal reduction here would blunt the measurable effect of the planned sensitivity change and would leave the actual cause untreated. No change is supported.

Evidence: local hour 19 carries the highest daytime time below range at 15.3 percent with a mean of 105.4 mg/dL and a minimum of 41 mg/dL, and it contains the sustained cluster of 48, 41 and 41 mg/dL on 2026-08-14. Uncertainty: those readings occurred roughly two to three hours after a 234 mg/dL peak that triggered a 4 U/h temporary basal request and boosted microbolus dosing, so the insulin causing them was delivered earlier and elsewhere, not by this basal segment. Dependencies: the correct lever is the high-glucose aggressiveness addressed in the sensitivity recommendation, and changing basal here would mask that test. Revisit if the evening lows persist unchanged after the sensitivity observation period.

Evidence: zero carbohydrates were logged in 14 days, carb_treatment_entries is empty, and carbohydrate-on-board was zero in all 24 sampled loop statuses, so this ratio never influenced a bolus. The only related observation is that the loop reports 13.3 g/U in the overnight window against the profile 13.0 g/U across three samples, a difference of about 2 percent. Uncertainty: that small offset is not evidence of a wrong value and may reflect rounding or a percentage applied by the running build. Dependencies: verification requires announced carbohydrates, which the morning logging recommendation would begin to provide. No change is supported.

Evidence: the loop reads this value correctly, reporting 11.1 g/U in the corresponding local hours, but with zero carbohydrate entries it has never been exercised in a meal bolus. Uncertainty: no announced-meal outcome exists anywhere in the period, so the accuracy of this ratio is entirely unknown rather than suspected. Dependencies: blocked until carbohydrates are logged. No change is supported.

Evidence: this segment covers the morning rise from 110.5 to 148.0 mg/dL between 08:00 and 10:00 local, but that rise was handled entirely by UAM with no carbohydrate entry, so the ratio played no part in it. The loop reports 13.2 g/U correctly in multiple statuses. Uncertainty: the morning pattern is a strategy consequence of reactive dosing, not evidence about ratio accuracy. Dependencies: this is the specific segment that the recommended morning carbohydrate logging would make testable first, because the morning window carries 0.0 percent time below range at 08:00 and 09:00. No change is supported until that data exists.

Evidence: this is the strongest ratio in the profile and it covers the afternoon plateau from 16:00 to 20:00 local, but it was never used because no carbohydrates were announced. Uncertainty: the afternoon highs cannot be attributed to this ratio, and the following evening lows suggest that any future announced dosing in this window should be approached cautiously rather than strengthened. Dependencies: blocked until carbohydrates are logged, and the afternoon window is explicitly deprioritized for meal experimentation. No change is supported.

Evidence: the evening rise between 20:00 and 22:00 local is modest, with means of 117.0, 120.0 and 127.6 mg/dL, and no carbohydrates were announced in this or any other window. Uncertainty: with no announced meals, the ratio is untested. Dependencies: blocked until carbohydrates are logged. No change is supported.

Evidence: the flat 56 mg/dL/U is a base value that dynamic sensitivity scales into an effective range of 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U, roughly twice as strong as profile above 200 mg/dL and roughly half as strong below 100 mg/dL. The most aggressive values coincide with the crashes, including sensitivity of 37.9 mg/dL/U with insulinReq of 1.98 units on 2026-08-19 and 27.8 mg/dL/U with insulinReq of 2.12 units on 2026-08-21. Uncertainty: profile ISF and the 70 percent dynamic factor multiply into the same effective number and cannot be separated from this data, and weakening the base value would also weaken the already-mild low-glucose behavior where effective sensitivity is 108 to 124 mg/dL/U. Dependencies: this row is explicitly held in reserve as the fallback lever behind the dynamic factor change, and changing both would make the result uninterpretable. Revisit only if the sensitivity factor reduction proves insufficient after at least 10 days.

Evidence: this target covers 00:00 to 08:00 local, where time below range is elevated in hours 00 to 03 at 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent but excellent in hours 04 to 07. Uncertainty: the loop is already applying its own target modulation, with observed values from 80 to 116 mg/dL against the three declared profile targets, through a mechanism absent from the supplied settings. Raising the profile target would interact unpredictably with that modulation and would also mask, rather than resolve, the insulin-tail explanation for the early-overnight lows. Dependencies: the target modulation conflict must be understood before any profile target change is meaningful. No change is supported.

Evidence: this target covers 08:00 to 23:00 local, the window containing both the daytime highs and the evening lows. Loop statuses in these hours report effective targets of 80, 82, 87, 90, 99, 104, 108 and 116 mg/dL, so the declared 100 mg/dL is frequently not the value in use. Uncertainty: the declared autosens_lowers_target is false, yet targets fall to 80 mg/dL during high and rising glucose, which is a direct conflict between declared settings and observed behavior that this package cannot resolve. Dependencies: adjusting the profile target while an undocumented modulation is active would produce an uninterpretable result. No change is supported, and the conflict is reported instead.

Evidence: local hour 23 shows a mean of 105.7 mg/dL with 88.7 percent in range, 10.1 percent below range and 1.2 percent above range, at the start of the overnight hypoglycemia cluster. Uncertainty: as with the other target rows, the lows here are better explained by the decaying insulin tail from evening dosing than by the target value, and the loop applies its own modulation regardless. Dependencies: tied to the same unresolved target-modulation mechanism and to the DIA question. No change is supported.

Evidence: a 10-hour DIA is mechanistically consistent with the repeated late declines in the therapy response windows, including minus 68 mg/dL at 240 minutes from a 0.05-unit bolus and minus 67 and minus 66 mg/dL at 240 and 360 minutes from a 0.2-unit bolus, and with the recurrent negative insulin on board of minus 0.481, minus 0.197 and minus 0.159 units after prolonged zero temporary basals. Uncertainty: DIA is confounded with the steepened dynamic sensitivity, with microbolus stacking at a 3-minute interval and with the insulin peak time, which is not supplied in the package, and no isolated DIA test exists in the data. Dependencies: shortening DIA would change insulin-on-board accounting across every other lever simultaneously and must not be combined with the planned sensitivity test. No change is supported now.

Evidence: both components have non-null values, so verify is not applicable. With zero carbohydrate entries and carbohydrate-on-board of zero in all 24 sampled statuses, UAM is the only mechanism covering meals, and it delivers 86.0 percent time in range without any carbohydrate announcement. UAM is not duplicating carbohydrate-on-board counting here because carbohydrate-on-board is genuinely zero throughout. Uncertainty: the aggressiveness of the UAM response is a concern, but that is governed by the boost logic, the sensitivity factor and the microbolus caps, not by these two on-off switches. Dependencies: disabling either would remove all meal coverage and would worsen the daytime highs without addressing the overcorrection cause. No change is supported.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB activation conditions (smb_always_enabled, smb_with_cob_enabled, smb_after_carbs_enabled, smb_with_temp_target_enabled, smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: all five components have non-null values, so verify is not applicable. The group is internally coherent: smb_always_enabled true makes the two carbohydrate-conditional flags inert in the current data, and smb_with_temp_target_enabled true with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false means microboluses are suppressed while a high temporary target runs, which occurred during the 180-minute 135 mg/dL targets on 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18. Uncertainty: 2026-08-18 shows both the highest time below range at 12.8 percent and 15.3 percent above range, so that suppression window contributes to variability, but it appears to be deliberate hypoglycemia-avoidance behavior rather than a misconfiguration. Dependencies: changing these flags would alter when microboluses occur and would confound the planned sensitivity test, which addresses how large they are. No change is supported.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB strength and frequency (smb_interval_minutes, max_smb_basal_minutes, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes)
parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: all three components have non-null values, so verify is not applicable. The 3-minute interval is taken from the configured setting and not from any waiting message, and it is a standard value. The caps compute to 0.18 to 0.20 units and 0.23 to 0.27 units at the current basal rates, and the loop reports exactly these as standardMaxBolus. Uncertainty: delivery demonstrably exceeds them, with standardMaxBolus 0.2 followed by a 0.4-unit microbolus on 2026-08-07, Increased SMB as percentage on 2026-08-18 and a 1.6-unit microbolus on 2026-08-19, driven by boost parameters that are not present in the supplied settings. Reducing these caps therefore has an unpredictable effect and could produce no benefit while consuming an observation cycle. Dependencies: this lever acts on the same effective dose as profile ISF and the dynamic sensitivity factor and must not be changed alongside either. It is held as the third-line option behind max IOB and the sensitivity factor.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits (max_basal_u_per_hour, max_iob_units)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: both components have non-null values, so verify is not applicable and a supported change exists. max_iob of 25 units stands against roughly 19.7 units of bolus and microbolus insulin per day and a peak observed insulin on board of 5.935 units on 2026-08-21, so the ceiling is one to two days of insulin and is never approached. It therefore provides no practical backstop against the large high-glucose requests observed, insulinReq 1.98 units on 2026-08-19 and 2.12 units on 2026-08-21. A value of 10 units retains substantial headroom above every observed value while restoring a meaningful limit. max_basal is deliberately left at 12 U/h because it is not the binding constraint: the logs show adj. req. rate 5.9 to maxSafeBasal 4, so the real 4.0 to 4.2 U/h ceiling comes from max_daily_safety_multiplier of 5 and current_basal_safety_multiplier of 6, which lie outside this group. Uncertainty: the appropriate max IOB depends on the user's usual peak insulin on board across a longer period than the 24 sampled statuses, so the candidate value must be checked against the user's own records before use. Dependencies: this is the only lever that confounds no other test, which is why it is sequenced first and alone.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / Autosens and Dynamic ISF (autosens_enabled, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled, autosens_raises_target, autosens_lowers_target, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: all five components have non-null values, so verify is not applicable. Effective sensitivity spans 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U around the flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U and becomes roughly twice as strong as profile above 200 mg/dL. The strongest values coincide precisely with the overcorrection events: 37.9 mg/dL/U with 4.73 units on board before the fall from 264 to 96 mg/dL in 120 minutes on 2026-08-19, and 27.8 mg/dL/U with 5.935 units on board on 2026-08-21. Six of 24 therapy response windows fall below 70 mg/dL within 6 hours. Reducing the factor from 70 to 60 percent is a single, reversible step that blunts high-glucose aggressiveness while leaving the profile ISF anchor and the mild low-glucose behavior intact. Uncertainty: the observed target modulation from 80 to 116 mg/dL contradicts the declared autosens target flags and originates in boost logic absent from the supplied settings, so part of the aggressiveness may not respond to this factor; sensitivity_ratio values of 0.79 to 1.0 are read as neutral or mild current adjustments, not as a disabled function. Dependencies: this must not be changed together with profile ISF or the microbolus caps, which act on the same effective dose, and it should follow the completed max IOB observation period.

Evidence: both components have non-null values, so verify is not applicable. Both settings are functionally inert in this dataset because carbohydrate-on-board was zero in every sampled loop status and no carbohydrate entry exists, so neither value has ever been exercised. min_5m_carbimpact of 8 is the standard value and meal_max_absorption_hours of 7 is only slightly above the usual 6. Uncertainty: the package contains no evidence at all about either value, and no duration is inferred from any aggregate average, since average_extended_carb_duration_min is null. Dependencies: changing an untested parameter would add noise to the sequential validation of the max IOB and sensitivity changes. These become testable only after the recommended morning carbohydrate logging produces real carbohydrate-on-board. No change is supported.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Keep the present approach unchanged for now: no prebolus, no immediate bolus percentage, full reliance on SMB and UAM, and no extended carbohydrate entries. Do not introduce any of these in the same period as an insulin-setting change. The system currently achieves 86.0 percent time in range with zero carbohydrate announcement, but it does so reactively, letting glucose rise first, which produces 20.2 percent above range at 10:00 and 32.1 percent at 16:00 local, and then applies a large late catch-up dose under a steepened effective sensitivity and a lowered effective target, which lands two to four hours later as hypoglycemia at 18:00 and 19:00 local. Prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage and extended carbohydrate parameters cannot responsibly be set from this package, because the user declaration contains an empty meal_strategies array and no carbohydrates were logged, so the meal domain should stay unchanged while the automation levers are tested one at a time.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Declared strategy, telemetry and inference agree rather than conflict here, which is why the conclusion is stable even though confidence is low. The declaration in aaps_profile.analysis_context is user-sourced and present, dated 2026-08-21T21:08:10Z, but meal_strategies is an empty array, period_exceptions is null and strategy_stable_for_period is null; because it is not true, no representative declaration can be assigned to the period. Telemetry matches: zero carbohydrate entries, zero grams, zero extended carbohydrate entries, is_extended_carbs false in all 24 therapy response windows, and carbohydrate-on-board of zero in all 24 sampled loop statuses. The consequence is that every meal is handled as a correction against unattributed rising glucose, so effective sensitivity of 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U and the modulated target between 80 and 116 mg/dL carry the entire meal load in place of the carb ratio, producing catch-up requests of 1.98 and 2.12 units on top of 4.73 and 5.935 units already on board. The 12:00 to 17:00 plateau has the shape associated with slow absorption, but meal, insulin-on-board, microbolus, temporary-target and correction effects cannot be separated with the data present, and GLP-1 dosed every three days on 2026-08-14, 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-20 is an unquantifiable confounder on gastric emptying, so no extended carbohydrate conclusion is drawn. Extended carbohydrate entries are also not a pump extended bolus; they create carbohydrate-on-board so the absorption model can act, which would activate min_5m_carbimpact and meal_max_absorption_hours, two settings that have never been exercised.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log the carbohydrate amount and the entry timestamp for the morning meal only, between 08:00 and 10:00 local, every day for 7 to 10 days while changing no insulin settings. That single action produces the first announced-meal outcomes in this dataset, separates the carb ratio of 13.2 g/U from UAM behavior, makes prebolus timing and immediate bolus percentage measurable for the first time, and exercises the two absorption settings under observation. It is the observation that unblocks more of this analysis than any other.

exceptions.pattern: Morning window 08:00 to 10:00 local, the only clean and reproducible meal signature: a stable 99.5 mg/dL baseline at 07:00 rising to a mean of 148.0 mg/dL by 10:00, with 0.0 percent time below range at 08:00 and 09:00 and 1.2 percent at 10:00.
exceptions.suggestion: Treat this as the window in which any future carbohydrate logging or prebolus experimentation is attempted first, once the automation observation periods are complete.
exceptions.rationale: A dosing or logging error here has almost no historical hypoglycemia consequence, and the window sits under a single carb ratio segment of 13.2 g/U and a single declared target of 100 mg/dL, so only one variable moves at a time and the result is interpretable.

exceptions.pattern: Afternoon plateau 14:00 to 17:00 local, with the highest time above range of the day at 26.3, 23.6, 32.1 and 22.6 percent, sitting directly upstream of the highest evening time below range at 7.7 and 15.3 percent.
exceptions.suggestion: Do not add meal aggressiveness, earlier dosing or extended carbohydrate entries in this window until the sensitivity and max IOB changes have been observed.
exceptions.rationale: Every documented crash originates here, on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, 2026-08-16 and 2026-08-19, and the falls of 168 to 178 mg/dL cannot be attributed to the logged boluses of 0.2 to 0.65 units, so the insulin already arriving in this window is boosted microbolus and temporary basal up to 4 U/h. More insulin here would most plausibly deepen the evening lows.

implementation_steps: Step 0, before changing anything: review this analysis with your diabetes care team, and independently confirm from your own AAPS records that the values reproduced here match your live setup, in particular max_iob of 25 units, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent of 70, profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, DIA of 10 hours, and the basal total of 16.2 units per day.

Step 1, discuss with the care team the two sustained hypoglycemia clusters, 51 to 42 mg/dL on 2026-08-13 from 17:59 to 18:14 local and 48 to 41 mg/dL on 2026-08-14 from 19:04 to 19:14 local, together with the period time below range of 5.1 percent, and agree on hypoglycemia treatment and alert settings before any parameter is altered.

Step 2, raise separately with the care team that the real temporary basal ceiling of 4.0 to 4.2 U/h comes from max_daily_safety_multiplier of 5 and current_basal_safety_multiplier of 6, not from max_basal of 12 U/h. Agree whether these belong in the plan before assessing the sensitivity change, since rates of 3.2, 3.6 and 4.0 U/h preceded the 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-19 events.

Step 3, if agreed, make the max IOB change alone, from 25 units toward a value such as 10 units that still sits well above your own highest observed insulin on board. Change nothing else. Observe for at least 7 days and record whether any loop decision was ever limited by the new value.

Step 4, review the observation period. Confirm that routine dosing was unaffected and note time below range at 18:00 and 19:00 local, currently 7.7 and 15.3 percent, and at 23:00 to 03:00 local, currently 10.1 to 18.5 percent, as the baseline for the next step.

Step 5, if agreed, reduce dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent from 70 to 60 as a single change. Do not alter profile ISF, the microbolus caps, basal, targets or DIA at the same time. Observe for at least 10 days.

Step 6, evaluate the sensitivity change specifically against the effective variable_sens values recorded at glucose above 200 mg/dL, the size of insulinReq at high glucose, the number of therapy response windows falling below 70 mg/dL within 6 hours, currently 6 of 24, and time above range at 16:00 local, currently 32.1 percent.

Step 7, if the evening and overnight lows persist after step 6, discuss with the care team which single fallback lever to test next, choosing one only: profile ISF at 56 mg/dL/U, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes at 20 minutes, or basal at 19:00 currently 0.7 U/h. Do not combine them.

Step 8, in parallel with observation but not in the same week as a parameter change, begin logging the carbohydrate amount and entry timestamp for the morning meal only, 08:00 to 10:00 local, for 7 to 10 days. This unblocks carb ratio, prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage and the two absorption settings for the next review.
Step 9, keep every change reversible and documented with its date, and stop and revert if hypoglycemia frequency or severity increases at any point rather than continuing to the next step.
education: Time below range of 5.1 percent sits above the commonly cited target of under 4 percent, while time in range of 86.0 percent and a coefficient of variation of 32.6 percent are both good. In an automated system, reducing lows and preserving time in range often means changing when insulin arrives rather than how much arrives in total.

When carbohydrates are never announced, unannounced meal detection must first see glucose rise before it can dose. That structurally produces a higher peak followed by a larger catch-up dose, so daytime highs in this pattern are usually a consequence of the strategy rather than proof that basal or the carb ratio is wrong.

Dynamic sensitivity scales a flat profile ISF according to current glucose. Here that produces an effective range of 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U from a base of 56, meaning corrections are roughly twice as strong at high glucose. Because the base value and the adjustment factor multiply into the same number, only one of them should be changed at a time or the result cannot be interpreted.

A long duration of insulin action means small doses continue acting for many hours. In this data, declines of 60 to 70 mg/dL appear at 240 and 360 minutes after boluses of only 0.05 to 0.2 units, and negative insulin on board appears after long zero temporary basals, which is why lows several hours after a correction should be traced back to the earlier dose rather than to the basal rate active at the time of the low.

A maximum insulin-on-board limit is a backstop, not a dosing parameter. Set far above normal operation, as with 25 units against a peak observed value of 5.935 units, it never engages. Set close to but above the usual peak, it does not change routine dosing but does cap an unusual sequence.

Extended carbohydrate entries are not the same as a pump extended bolus. They create carbohydrate-on-board over a declared duration so the loop's absorption model can respond, whereas an extended bolus schedules insulin directly. Using them activates the carbohydrate absorption settings, which in this period have never been exercised.

A sensitivity ratio of 1 in a loop status means the current adjustment is neutral, not that a sensitivity function is switched off. In this data the ratio varies between 0.79 and 1.0, showing a live sensitivity computation.

Context entries matter for interpretation: the occlusion and pump error on 2026-08-19, the sensor changes on 2026-08-11 and 2026-08-21, and GLP-1 dosed every three days on 2026-08-14, 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-20 can all shift glucose patterns independently of settings, which is why an isolated 42 mg/dL reading shortly before a sensor change is treated differently from a sustained multi-reading low.

Make only one change at a time and allow a full observation period, at least 7 days for the max IOB step and at least 10 days for the sensitivity step, before considering the next one. Changing dependent settings together makes the outcome uninterpretable.

No change should be made to AAPS automatically or on the basis of this analysis alone; you remain in control of every setting and are responsible for confirming that each candidate value is appropriate for you.

Two sustained level-2 lows occurred in this period, reaching 42 mg/dL on 2026-08-13 and 41 mg/dL on 2026-08-14. Ensure hypoglycemia treatment is available and alert thresholds are appropriate before altering any insulin-delivery setting.
